To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) DNMT1 deficiency in human cells leads to a drop in MMR proteins levels, 2) this effect is mediated through the DNA damage response (DDR) and 3) the DDR is mediated through PARP.
DNMT1 deficiency in normal human fibroblast cells triggers microsatellite instability through depletion of MMR protein levels in a DNA damage response dependent process involving PARP overactivation.
DNMT1 depletion triggers mismatch repair defects through decreased repair protein levels in an indirect process involving the DNA-damage response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of DNA methyltransferase DNMT1 and the DNA damage response in the regulation of microsatellite instability.
understanding the molecular mechanism by which DNA methylation is involved in the maintenance of genomic integrity.
the epigenetics of DNA repair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the loss of DNMT1 in hTERT 1605 cells results in a decrease in MMR components, and that this effect is not due to transcriptional silencing but rather due to the activation of the DNA Damage Response and PARP overactivation.
DNMT1 deficiency leads to mismatch repair defects in normal human cells through depletion, via the DNA damage response, of repair protein levels.
DNMT1 is required to maintain steady state protein levels of MMR genes, and in the absence of DNMT1 these levels fall due to the DNA damage response, resulting in microsatellite instability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNMT1 deficiency leads to MMR defects by a mechanism involving the DDR, which in turn is triggered by depletion of MMR proteins.
DNMT1 is a key player in stabilizing microsatellite repeats, and that this function is not limited to stem cells but also applies to differentiated cells.
DNMT1 is a critical component of a pathway that maintains steady state levels of key MMR components and that the DNA damage response is a key regulator of this pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNMT1 depletion triggers mismatch repair defects, likely through depletion of repair component levels.
DNMT1 is not just a maintenance methylase, but is also involved in the regulation of other processes, including MMR, and that the effect of DNMT1 knock down is not confined to stem cells.
a decrease in DNMT1 protein level can cause MMR deficiency through a decrease in MMR component levels.
